name: What kind of foundation do tiny homes require?

mainEntity.name: What kind of foundation do tiny homes require?

acceptedAnswer.text: The foundation type for a tiny home depends on its classification and the site conditions. Permanent tiny homes typically require a traditional foundation, such as a concrete slab, perimeter stem wall, or pier and beam, adhering to local building codes. Tiny homes on wheels are not permanently affixed and use their integrated trailer chassis as a 'foundation' for mobility, though they might sit on blocking or temporary supports when parked. For stability and long-term placement, many choose to level and secure even wheeled units, sometimes with skirting or decking. The choice impacts cost, permanence, and ease of relocation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permanent tiny homes use traditional foundations (slab, stem wall, pier/beam) per building codes. Tiny homes on wheels use their chassis for mobility, but may use temporary supports when parked.
